newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index drops on continued profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index drops on continued profit-taking.

text.p: Most Hungarian shares on Tuesday consolidated at around Monday's levels, but continued profit-taking pushed the BUX index, which is calculated from average prices, slightly down, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 3,490.44 points, down 15.22.
"Profit-taking continued, but already at a slower pace than yesterday," said Gabor Borda of Concorde Securities.
"The prices of the most important papers rose, but this was the upward correction of a declining trend," MKB Securities' Peter Lencs said.
Hungarian shares soared for most of the year, and with the year-end approaching, it was logical that profit-takings would shave off some of the market's gains, dealers said.
They added that they expected the declinig trend to continue for at least the next few days, but price falls could be mixed with upward corrections, as it happened gn Tuesday.

Analysts said on Tuesday that not recent mixed earnings from Hungarian companies inspired foreign investors to take profits, rather the 2,000 point gain in the bourse this year to over 3,500 points meant some were locking in gains.

The price of drug maker EGIS EGIS.BU and hotel chain Danubius rose, as a correction following sharp recent falls, dealers said. Egis closed at 8,000 forints, up 100 forints while Danubius ended at 3,205, up 75.

The price of oil company MOL was also corrected slightly upward. The stock, which closed at 1,655, up 20,8had positive outlook, as Hungary was expected to decide on next year's energy price rises on Thursday, traders said.
Chemicals maker Borsodchem, however, dropped 70 forints on Tuesday and closed at 3,300 forints.
BUX index futures closed lower by 35 to 65 points. The settlement price of the December maturity closed at 3,615.5 points, down 47.5 pgints.
